newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods ease with local demand, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods ease with local demand, NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices eased as weak New York futures and thin local demand combined to keep buyers from the market, traders said.
Flooding in California's central valley kept motorists off roads and caused inventories to pile up at terminals, brokers said.
"We're still fighting (low) terminal demand, which is way down because of weather," a broker said.
Products for prompt January delivery were seen two cents lower than February supplies, due to weak demand, traders said.
Dealers said they failed to strike any deals because many buyers and sellers left early for the weekend.
Conventional unleaded in San Francisco shed a half cent from Thursday, with bids 74 cents a gallon, and offers 75 cents. Premium gasoline held a seven cent advantage.
CARB-grade gasoline in the Bay fetched 75.50/76.25 cents a gallon, down about a cent, as NYMEX gasoline eased 0.33 cents to 70.15 cents.
"I think it's going to be weak here next week," said a broker, adding that receding floodwaters made marketers unsure if demand would improve.
